title: Tetzaveh: names over the heart (Exodus 28:12, 29)
hookLine: the high priest carries the tribes' names on his shoulders and over his heart

lines: A WHOLE PEOPLE, ON HIS CLOTHES.
cards: Some people keep a list of names. A grandmother who prays every night through her grandchildren, one by one, oldest to youngest. A nurse who keeps the first names of patients she's lost on a folded card in her wallet.

A soldier with a buddy's name on a bracelet. The high priest of Israel was asked to carry an entire people this way, on his clothes, every time he went into the sanctuary. Twice over, in two different places on his body.

teach.h: TWO ONYX STONES, SIX AND SIX.
teach.b: First, the shoulders. On the ephod, the high priest's apron, there are two shoulder straps, and on each sits an onyx stone.

Engraved on the two stones, six and six, are the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, in the order they were born. The verse says Aaron shall bear their names before the LORD upon his two shoulders for a memorial.
Hanging in front of his chest is the breastplate, the choshen: a square of woven cloth set with twelve precious stones in four rows of three, each engraved with one tribe's name.
In the old Jewish translation: "And Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment upon his heart." The same twelve names, carried in two places.
Some readers have dwelt on the difference.

teach.h: SHOULDERS FOR WEIGHT, HEART FOR LOVE.
teach.b: The shoulders are where you carry weight: a burden, a responsibility.

teach.h: ON THE HEART, ONE BY ONE.
teach.b: The heart is where you carry love: the people as people you care about. A leader needs both. Only shoulders, and the people become a weight.
Only heart, and nothing gets carried. And one more thing. On the shoulders, two big stones hold six names each.
On the heart, every tribe gets its own stone. Nobody is grouped. Each name is held one by one, and every time Aaron went in before God, he walked in wearing them all.

how: Jews pray for the sick by name, often in the Mi Sheberakh prayer said during the Torah reading, where people call out the names of those who need healing, and in the Amidah's blessing for healing.

o: you shall command: the portion that dresses the high priest
the high priest's breastplate with its twelve stones
a list of the tribes in the order they were born

games.q: the names the high priest carried — tap the pairs.

s: the tribes' names appeared only once on the high priest's clothes
twice: on the shoulder stones and on the breastplate.
on the breastplate, each tribe had its own stone
twelve stones in four rows of three, one name on each.
the shoulder stones were engraved with the names in birth order
six and six, according to their birth.

games.q: you're the high priest, about to go into the holy place. what do you carry over your heart?
o: the names of the twelve tribes.
games.why: the names of the children of Israel, in the breastplate, upon his heart, one stone for each.

practice: Let a few names come to mind, people who need carrying right now: someone sick, someone grieving, someone just starting something hard. Say each name slowly, on its own, without grouping them.
If you pray, hold each one before God the way Aaron carried them; if not, let each name rest, for a breath, over your heart.
